summary: Round 4, scoped to the delta since 19d8ae11daa3. Both round-3 items are fixed and MEASURED fixed. (T2) `isEntryKey("bins.delta")` kills the narrowing mutant `startsWith(logPrefix)` -> `startsWith(prefix)`, and it is the ONLY one of the three assertions in that method that does; it passes on the unmutated tree. (T1) removing `isEntryKey("")` dropped no coverage: with it gone, deleting `!key.startsWith(logPrefix)` is still killed (by `.delta` AND by `bins.delta`) and deleting `!key.endsWith(SUFFIX)` is still killed (uniquely by `logPrefix() + "x"`), as is deleting both guards. Method used: apply the mutant, `rm -rf sequencer/build/test-results/test`, run the full 254-test :sequencer:test, parse the JUnit XML for failures; plus a per-assertion kill matrix built by compiling three variants of the method each retaining a single assertion. One new gap found, symmetric to the one just closed: the endsWith guard is pinned against DELETION but not against NARROWING. Three further survivors (m5, m7, m9) are argued EQUIVALENT rather than reported as gaps. No existing test file is touched by this diff at all, so testing.md rules 4-5 are satisfied by inspection. Tiers are right (LogKeysTest is T0 and pure; ChainReplayNonDeltaKeyTest is T1 on MemoryBinStore), no sleep, no port, no system temp. Tree restored: `git diff --cached` sha256 6e889cf0920b907a6c04bedc807b35699f7f1df074bc53468f70542d9547838f, :sequencer:test resolved FROM-CACHE (byte-identical inputs), `./gradlew test` BUILD SUCCESSFUL.

findings.title: The endsWith guard is pinned against deletion but not against NARROWING -- the exact asymmetry the same method just fixed for startsWith
findings.detail: SURVIVING MUTATION, measured against the full :sequencer:test (254 tests, all green): `key.endsWith(SUFFIX)` -> `key.endsWith("delta")`. Also survives as `key.endsWith("a")`. Any suffix of ".delta" works, because every real key still ends with it and the substring still slices `key.length() - SUFFIX.length()`. FAILURE SCENARIO, reachable today by the same argument the method's own comment makes for the length guards: a foreign object named `<logPrefix>delta` (or `<logPrefix>data`, `<logPrefix>meta` under the `"a"` form) comes back from `store.list(logPrefix, ...)`, passes the narrowed guard, and reaches `key.substring(32, 31)`. Measured under the mutant with a throwaway probe: `PROBE delta -> THREW java.lang.StringIndexOutOfBoundsException: Range [32, 31) out of bounds for length 37`; on the unmutated tree the same key answers `false`. That unchecked exception propagates out of `chainEnd`/`applyChain`, makes the takeover throw and `LocalSequencer.start` release the lease -- the forever-loop this task exists to remove -- so it is in scope for M4.8b1 rather than adjacent to it. WHY THE THREE EXISTING CASES MISS IT: `.delta` and `bins.delta` do not start with `logPrefix` so they die at the first guard; `logPrefix() + "x"` does not end with any suffix of ".delta", so it pins the guard's PRESENCE and not its OPERAND. Its `.as()` text, "pins the endsWith guard", is therefore true as written but the method now pins the startsWith operand explicitly and the endsWith operand not at all. FIX IF WANTED, one assertion, measured rather than proposed: `assertThat(KEYS.isEntryKey(KEYS.logPrefix() + "delta")).as("pins the endsWith OPERAND").isFalse();` -- PASSES on the unmutated tree, FAILS under both `endsWith("delta")` and `endsWith("a")`. RECOMMENDATION: record it, do not fix it. Under review.md `minors-land` a minor on a pass is recorded in the commit body and the commit lands, and this task's own `rounds:M4.8b1` argument says every round since round 2 was spent on prose introduced by the previous round's fix. One more assertion buys one more paragraph of comment to be wrong about.
findings.failure_scenario: A foreign object named `<logPrefix>delta` is returned by `store.list(logPrefix, ...)` -- flat and undelimited, so any name comes back. Under the surviving mutant `key.endsWith(SUFFIX)` -> `key.endsWith("delta")` it passes both guards and reaches `key.substring(32, 31)`, which throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException (measured: `Range [32, 31) out of bounds for length 37`) out of `chainEnd`/`applyChain`. The takeover throws, `LocalSequencer.start` releases the lease, the next node repeats, forever -- the exact loop M4.8b1 exists to remove -- and the whole 254-test :sequencer:test suite is green throughout. On the unmutated tree the same key answers `false`.

findings.title: `isEntryKey(".delta")` has no unique kill among the mutants generated -- subsumed by `bins.delta`
findings.detail: PER-ASSERTION KILL MATRIX, each variant compiled with exactly one of the three assertions retained and run as `--tests LogKeysTest`. A = `".delta"`, B = `logPrefix() + "x"`, C = `"bins.delta"`. startsWith narrowed to `prefix`: A survives, B survives, C KILLS. startsWith deleted: A kills, B survives, C kills. endsWith deleted: A survives, B KILLS, C survives. Both guards deleted: all three kill. So B is the sole killer of the endsWith deletion and C the sole killer of the startsWith narrowing, while everything A kills, C also kills. This is NOT the round-3 `isEntryKey("")` finding repeating -- A does kill two mutants in isolation, so it is not decoration; I simply could not construct a guard mutation that A kills and C does not, and I have not proved none exists. Keeping A costs nothing and its `.as()` text is accurate. Recorded so the next session does not spend a round re-deriving the matrix.
findings.failure_scenario: No production failure: this is a redundancy note, not a gap. If assertion C (`bins.delta`) were ever deleted in a later refactor believing A (`.delta`) covered the same ground, the `startsWith(logPrefix)` -> `startsWith(prefix)` narrowing would go unpinned again -- A survives it. Recorded so the kill matrix does not have to be re-derived to see that A and C are not interchangeable in that direction.

findings.title: Three further survivors are argued EQUIVALENT rather than reported as test gaps
findings.detail: Reported so they are not rediscovered and mistaken for holes. (1) Both guards replaced by `if (key.length() < logPrefix.length() + SUFFIX.length()) return false;` -- survives. Equivalent: the function can only return true via `key.equals(keyFor(sequence))`, which already implies both `startsWith(logPrefix)` and `endsWith(SUFFIX)`, and the length test alone guarantees `begin <= end` in the substring, so neither the return value nor the throw behaviour changes. (2) `!key.startsWith(logPrefix)` replaced by `key.length() < logPrefix.length()` -- survives; the residual throw needs a key under `logPrefix` shorter than `logPrefix.length() + 6` that still ends in ".delta", which is impossible because `logPrefix` ends in '/' and that slot would have to hold a character of ".delta". (3) `catch (NumberFormatException) { return false; }` replaced by `catch { sequence = 0; }` -- survives; `keyFor(0)`'s digits are hex by construction, so a key whose digits did not parse cannot equal it. The corollary is that the two guards carry no semantics beyond preventing the StringIndexOutOfBoundsException -- which is exactly what the method's comment at line 69-72 claims, so the comment is accurate and T3 is precisely the untested half of it.
findings.failure_scenario: No production failure claimed -- the opposite. These three mutants survive the suite and I am arguing they are EQUIVALENT rather than reporting them as holes, because an unargued survivor list is how a real defect gets laundered as known-benign (the failure `rounds:M4.8a` records). If any of the three arguments is wrong, the failure scenario is whichever of `key.equals(keyFor(sequence))`'s implications I got wrong: a key that returns true without starting with `logPrefix`, or a short key reaching `begin > end`. I checked both by construction and neither is reachable.
